Q: Model with nested effect returning NA coefficients A:

First Model

We can try this code:

library(emmeans)
fm <- lm(value ~ CI * Year, md)
em <- emmeans(fm, ~ Year | CI)
contrast(em, list(BA = c(0.5, 0.5, -0.5, -0.5)))

Here fm is the linear model object and from that we get the emmeans object em. These emmeans contain predictions (and other info). For example the first one is the following. It gives the same value as in the emmean column of the first row of the em object.

predict(fm, list(CI = "Control", Year = "2021"))

There are 8 such predictions because there are 2 CI levels and 4 Year levels so there are 2 * 4 = 8 combinations.

The first line in the output of the constrast statement above gives the same result as this:

library(multcomp)
fmControl <- lm(value ~ Year + 0, md, subset = CI == "Control")
glht(fmControl, "0.5*Year2022 - 0.5*Year2023 - 0.5*Year2024 = 0")

Second Model

We can also try:

library(emmeans)
library(ggplot2)
fm2 <- lm(value ~ CI * BA, md)
em2 <- emmeans(fm2, ~ BA | CI)
cc <- contrast(em2, list(BA = c(1, -1))); cc
plot(cc)
pairs(emmeans(fm2, ~ BA | CI))
joint_tests(fm2)

In this case there are two levels to BA and two to CI so in a similar way there will be 4 predictions in em2 and in a similar way we can test the indicated contrast for each level of CI (and also plot them). In this case the contrasts are pairwise comparisons and emmeans provides a simpler function pairs that provides the contrasts for you.

Conceptually joint_tests works by balancing the data via ref_grid and then applying the anova function to that. This does not actually work because anova won't handle the zero residual but hopefully this gives the idea.

rg2 <- ref_grid(fm2)
md_bal <- as.data.frame(rg2)
fm3 <- lm(prediction ~ CI * BA, md_bal, weights = 1 / diag(vcov(rg2)),
  contrasts = list(CI = "contr.sum", BA = "contr.sum"))
anova(fm3, df = df.residual(fm2)) # does not work but this is the idea
joint_tests(fm2) # same

Q: Is putting new items in C++ std::map during a std::for_each() that traverses that same map a potential segfault (if reallocation happens)? A:

Modifying a std::map while iterating over it does not invalidate iterators.

Specifically for operator[] which you use, it is mentioned in the cppreference documentation:

No iterators or references are invalidated.

(other std::map modifying methods also guarantee validity of iterators - see e.g. std::map::insert, std::map::emplace etc.).

Therefore your code is valid in that respect.

Note:
As Igor commented, it is not guaranteed that newly added elements will be visited during the current traverse. But in this case it does not seem to matter.

Q: Improving structure of a Java base conversion program A:

I feel the structure has redundant logic, especially in conversion methods.

You can convert values directly from one base to another, bypassing conversion to decimal (from String to String).

How can I reduce duplication in methods like toDec() and fromDec()?

Just return sum from toDecSteps() function and take this value instead of calling toDec().

Is there a better object-oriented design for this kind of converter?

For example, your class can have current int value, getter: String getValue(int base) and setter: void setValue(String v, int base).
